chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Musanna al-Hannat, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon him) was seated, and a funeral passed by him. So the people stood up when the funeral emerged. So Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) said: 'A funeral of a Jew passed by, and the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was on its path, seated. So he disliked that the head of the deceased Jew be higher than his, therefore he stood up for that.'
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic etiquette regarding standing for a funeral, as demonstrated by the Prophet and Imam Al-Husayn?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* illustrates the profound humility (*tawadu'*) of the Ahl al-Bayt by linking Imam Al-Husayn’s practice to the Prophet Muhammad’s precedent. It highlights the specific etiquette of standing for non-Muslims during funerals, not out of reverence for their faith, but as a gesture of general respect and to avoid elevating the deceased above the standing person, a nuance valued in Shia fiqh.
